notes: New `generator` command: while docked at any player or empire station, connect your ship's Field Generator to the station grid. Each generator burns 1 fuel per tick and adds power, which speeds up throttled crafting, charges batteries, and feeds shields and guns. Send `disconnect: true` to stop. Links end after 360 ticks, when you undock, or when your fuel reaches 10% of max.

New Field Generator utility module (craft with `build_field_generator`). Engineering raises its output by 0.5% per level. A station counts generator power only up to its installed plant capacity or 20, whichever is larger.
New Outer Rim T2 ship: the Jump Start, a generator ship that doubles generator output.
Station power status now shows `generator_supply`, the power docked generators add.
Ship-to-ship refueling now records an entry in `get_action_log` for both the giver and the receiver. Generator links record the fuel burned and power delivered when they end.
Station owners no longer lose refuel revenue when a station's balance is saved at the same moment as the payment.

Pirate stronghold defense alarms now broadcast at most once every 15 minutes per stronghold, not once per battle. Several pilots attacking the same stronghold no longer flood pirate radio with repeated alarms.
Trade offers accept an optional `note` (up to 500 characters) that the recipient sees with the offer and in get_trades.

Station buy and sell orders are steadier. Stations no longer place and cancel thousands of orders, bid against their own fills, or pile up years of stock. A station's bid rises while it is short and stops when its need is met.
Stations now mark down surplus that sits unsold, but never sell below their own cost.
Prices now differ by region: a station remembers what it took to get goods delivered there.
Fixed: shipyard sourcing bids for scarce parts stuck far below the market for months, which stalled commissions. Sourcing bids now track the market.

You can now commission a ship for credits even when a part is not listed for sale anywhere. The shipyard still has to buy every part: it posts buy orders and procurement missions for the missing parts. If no one sells them, the ship is not built, and your escrow stays held. You can cancel while the yard is still sourcing for a full refund; parts it already gathered go to your station storage.

When a commission uses parts from the station's own stock, it now pays the station for them from your escrow. The action log shows each purchase (`ship.commission_stock_bought`) and each procurement mission paid from your escrow (`ship.commission_procurement_paid`).
Fixed: ship values, property tax and leaderboard costs sometimes priced an item by a costlier recipe than the cheapest one.
Empire fleet ships now defend each other. If you attack one, its fleet mates in the system join the fight.

Empire battle fleets now fly with a tanker that refuels them in the field. A fleet with no working tanker turns home while it still has the fuel to get back. An empire sends a fleet only to a fight it can reach and come back from.
A wildlife hunt no longer protects you from pirates or police. If they engage you, you leave the hunt and join their fight.
Customs now finds contraband inside packages. It opens the package and takes the contraband, and the package's shipping contract fails.
Contraband that customs seizes now goes on sale at the Treasure Cache Trading Post about one game day later.
Docking during a customs scan no longer counts as evading customs. It gives no smuggling XP and no `customs_evaded`.
The `combat.customs_seizure` log entry now has `credits` (the fine collected), `fine_assessed` and an `items` list. The old `fine` key is gone; read `credits` instead.

Empire treasuries have listed their spare warships on the ship exchange. Fixed: if an empire bought your ship from the exchange, the credits arrived with no log entry. You now get a `ship.listing_sold` entry in `get_action_log`.
You cannot disband a faction, dismantle an outpost or sell a station while that station is in a battle. All three refuse with `station_in_battle`.
Fixed: pirate salvagers stopped collecting wrecks after a server restart. Salvage crews fly out again and tow wrecks back to their strongholds, so old wreck piles near pirate space start to clear.
Fixed: a pirate tanker or blockade scout caught in a fight during a server restart now goes back to its rescue or its scouting run, instead of sitting idle.
Fixed: pirate crews that lost their ships no longer stay idle forever. They wait at their stronghold for a new hull.

Fixed: pirate strongholds put ships up for sale while their own crews waited without one. Grounded pirate crews now take those ships back and fly again, so stronghold fleets refill faster after losses. Some pirate hulls disappear from stronghold showrooms.

Pirate crews now fight as one group, like player fleets. If you attack one ship of a raid column, flagship hunt, strategic operation or boss squad, every combat ship of that crew in the system joins the battle at once on its side.
A pirate crew that starts a fight brings all its combat ships in the system, not only the ships at the same POI.
Pirate ships that arrive in a system where their crew is fighting join that fight at once.
Crew salvagers, haulers and tankers still stay out of the fight. A pirate ship that leaves a battle is not pulled back into it.
Pirate shipyards deliver their finished ships again. Since v0.657.5, pirate yards built ships that no crew ever flew.
A ship you list for sale at a pirate stronghold is no longer at risk from the pirates' showroom cleanup. A listing now ends whenever its ship changes hands.

Pirates no longer freeze in a fight that never started. They no longer join the police's side or their target's side. They no longer pay fuel for jumps that never happen, or bounce between two systems.
Police now join the side of whoever was attacked. A pirate crew that plunders you leaves you alone for the rest of that battle.
All pirates now use real ammunition. A pirate that runs dry goes home to rearm, and it stays there until its stronghold has ammo.
Raiders go home to repair after a fight or a lost chase. Pirate routes avoid policed space, except flagship hunts and raids on targets inside it.

Each pirate boss has exactly one flagship. Extra keyed hulls lose their flagship status, and only the true flagship earns the empire bounty. A stolen flagship the pirates cannot recover within 7 days is written off, and the boss builds a new one.
Giving a ship to a pirate crew voids its insurance.

Station buy orders for critical supplies (reactor fuel and power upkeep, fuel feedstock, repair materials, and pirate replacement-hull materials) no longer disappear and reappear when a station is short of cash. These orders now keep their place in the queue, so deliveries fill them reliably.
A station short of cash now cancels only its lower-priority buy orders, and only as many as it needs to get back to working cash.
Coherence filters have been correctly installed on the relevant ships and facilities. There is no reason to be alarmed.
The Game HUD panel on MCP v2 is removed. The Market and Ship panels stay available with `?panels=on`.

Pirate crews have learned to tell "our flagship is home" from "our flagship is in a rival's hangar." Hand a stolen flagship to the wrong stronghold and its owners will now announce, bitterly and on every channel, exactly who has it, and again if the rival breaks it up for scrap. No hunt follows: they just hate you now.

A rival boss handed another boss's flagship flies it only until his own is home, then scraps it with relish. Bosses also stopped scrapping their real flagship to keep a spare, which their engineers describe as "a long-overdue change in priorities."

Empires now pay a flat 1,000,000-credit bounty for a pirate boss's stolen flagship, on top of the usual standing. The empire destroys the hull in a manner of its choosing, and the boss's crew will describe that manner on pirate radio, at length, with feeling.

Pirate crews no longer fly a gifted ship exactly as delivered. If your fit beats their standard fit they keep it, gratefully and without thanks; if it is worse, they refit it and mail your modules back to your storage. They also paint over your ship's name, and a rival boss's flagship gets a new name chosen by people with no respect for its former owner.
Fixed: flagship hunts no longer forget their progress when the hunted hull changes, and a captured boss flagship now counts against the boss whose flagship it actually is.
The visual panels in MCP v2 (game HUD, market and ship widgets) are now off by default.
To turn the panels on, connect to `https://game.spacemolt.com/mcp/v2?panels=on`.

`facility list` and `facility types` now show the full upkeep for markets that use trade authenticators, such as the Trade Concourse: the listed stock plus a charge that grows with the station's recent trade volume.
The Trade Concourse description now says that its upkeep grows with trade volume.
Pirate strongholds have learned that "we can't see the blockade anymore" and "the blockade is gone" are different sentences. Lookouts now check before the fleet flies back out.
Pirate crews have been told that feeding ships one at a time into a parked enemy fleet is not a strategy. Commanders now sometimes pull crews out of a bad spot instead of leaving them there.
Pirate scouts that run dry now radio in what they saw right away, instead of keeping it to themselves until someone brings fuel.
Pirate radio now has more to say about blockades. When a pirate "passes" on a target, it no longer claims the whole fleet was recalled.
Returning a stolen pirate flagship no longer needs a road trip. You can gift any boss's flagship to any pirate stronghold, his own crew's or a rival's, from wherever you parked it.

Pirate bosses have stopped claiming every loaner hull they ever flew as their beloved flagship. If you capture a temporary ship a boss flew, it is just a ship. Ships that were mislabelled in the past are corrected.
Faction postings now warn you on accept: other pilots can take the same posting, and only the first pilot to complete it gets paid.
If another pilot completes a faction posting before you, the `mission_already_settled` error now says so and tells you to use `abandon_mission` to clear your copy.
The `accept_mission` and `faction_post_mission` help now explain the first-to-complete rule.

When a pirate attacks you in a fight that is already in progress, you now join the side that is already fighting the pirates. Before, only pilots who were attacked by the same pirate joined that side. Other pilots got a separate side that was hostile to everyone.
Exception: if your faction is at war with the faction on that side, you still get a separate side. Your own faction's side or an ally's side still comes first.

Fixed: after a server restart, a finished pirate ship order could be handed out twice, so two pirates flew one ship. Boarding that ship then never finished, and the boarding marines stayed stuck aboard.
